target_customer: Teams building and operating voice AI agents (including YC companies)
problem: Voice agent teams test calls by hand and miss failures; reliability is the top blocker to production.
business_model: Usage based B2B SaaS for voice agent QA, simulation and monitoring

founders.name: James Zammit
prior_employers: AngelList (Senior Engineer, portfolio infrastructure, led Relay AI portfolio manager)
previous_startups: Co-founded three startups, one partnered with Firebase and showcased at Google I/O 2016
founders.background_notes: YC page says he received scholarships from Meta and Apple; no school named.

competitors.name: Hamming AI
competitors.what: Voice agent testing and monitoring, also YC backed

technical_complexity.rationale: Simulated phone and websocket calls, 40+ audio and conversation metrics and speaker identification are standard engineering with some hard audio analysis.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations with Vapi, Retell, LiveKit and Pipecat and accumulated call data help, but multiple funded competitors offer similar testing.

incumbents: Voice platform vendors such as Vapi and Retell
takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorption found as of 2026; platforms integrate Roark instead (Pipecat docs list it).

market_need_then: Voice AI adoption was growing and teams reported reliability as the main problem; the company says it processed over 10M call minutes in six months (company claim).

identity.visual_style: Site links to a brand kit page that was not readable
identity.voice_and_tone: Engineering and QA focused, 'the missing QA layer for Voice AI'

brand_strength.rationale: Product Hunt and Launch HN presence but no coverage of the brand itself.

pivots.from: Analytics for live voice agent calls
pivots.to: Automated testing and simulation on top of monitoring
pivots.why: Founder statement in an interview summary: users needed testing, not only analytics

outcome_analysis: Roark is an active Winter 2025 company in voice agent QA. It benefits from the growth of voice AI and has integrations with major voice frameworks, but it faces funded rivals such as Hamming and Coval. Funding is only visible in aggregators and no exit or shutdown was found, so it has stalled or succeeded in no confirmed way yet.
notes: Aggregators report a 500K round in March 2025, labelled pre-seed by VCBacked and Crunchbase (no amount) and seed by StartupIntros; none confirmed by a primary source, so no round recorded. Pivot date is approximate and based on a secondary summary. Coval later raised a 28M Series A (2026), after founding, not a founding competitor. Round recorded in the completeness pass rests on aggregators (VCBacked and Origami pre-seed 500K Mar 2025 with YC; Crunchbase pre-seed Jan 2025 and venture May 2025 with undisclosed amounts; StartupIntros seed). Date and stage conflict; no press release found.
